messages.subject: Images in rApache
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am very new to rApache (installed it last night). First of all great
job everybody this is an exciting tool. I am working on an online demo
for a Kaplan-Meyer model ({survival} package). I am attaching the link
to my online application so you guys can see it. My problem right now
is that I don't exactly know how to deal with the followings:

1) plots and images
2) memory management

Basically I call an R script from an html file with javascript. This
java script loads the page in an invisible iFrame (I know it is
stupid) so the R file will update the image on the server. with the
same javascript I update the content of the <img> tag to that plot. My
kaplan meyer model takes some time so sometimes by the time I update
the img src the plot is not generated yet.

my questions are:
How can I make sure that my plot is there before updating it? what is
the best practice here?

also how can I detach a dataframe in my R script? It seems to me that
every time I attach a dataframe it stays in the memory for that
session and I cannot detach it. It gives me some unwanted warnings on
my page and I am wondering if there is any way to suppress them

Here is the link to my online demo:
http://siamak.banatao.berkeley.edu/extime/

again thanks for the hard work (if there is no Debian/Ubuntu package
for it yet I can focus on putting one together to contribute back to
the community)

Cheers
Mark

I used a javascript approach with prototype in the useR2007 example
(located in the rapache source dist). An AJAX call creates the plot
with R, saves the png to a image directory served by apache, and then
returns an html string containing an <img> tag filled out with the
image location. Prototype was used to display a spinner image while
all this was happenning on the server.

> also how can I detach a dataframe in my R script? It seems to me that
> every time I attach a dataframe it stays in the memory for that
> session and I cannot detach it. It gives me some unwanted warnings on
> my page and I am wondering if there is any way to suppress them

Just call detatch() before you return control over to apache. Simple
enough, right? Attaching a data frame seems heavy-handed if you're
just looking for convenient access to its variables. You might want to
scope out with(). It's very useful.
